title: Famous battles
blurb: Where the battles that shaped India were fought, by period.
source: Public facts (places and dates), listed by hand with the notes written for this site; positions taken from Wikidata where it has the place
licence: Facts, no copyright; positions from Wikidata (CC0)

items.name: Kalinga (Dhauli)
items.detail: 261 BCE: Ashoka conquers Kalinga; the suffering of the war turns him to Buddhism and dhamma.

items.name: Tarain
items.detail: 1191 and 1192: Prithviraj Chauhan beats Muhammad of Ghor in the first battle and loses to him in the second.

items.name: Panipat
items.detail: Three battles: 1526 (Babur beats Ibrahim Lodi), 1556 (Akbar's army beats Hemu) and 1761 (Ahmad Shah Abdali beats the Marathas).

items.name: Khanwa
items.detail: 1527: Babur defeats Rana Sanga's Rajput alliance.

items.name: Talikota
items.detail: 1565: the Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara, and Hampi is sacked.

items.name: Haldighati
items.detail: 1576: Maharana Pratap of Mewar fights Akbar's army led by Man Singh.

items.name: Chittorgarh
items.detail: Sieges of the fort in 1303 (Alauddin Khalji), 1535 (Bahadur Shah of Gujarat) and 1568 (Akbar).

items.name: Samugarh
items.detail: 1658: Aurangzeb defeats Dara Shikoh in the war of succession.

items.name: Plassey
items.detail: 1757: Robert Clive defeats Siraj ud-Daulah; the East India Company becomes the power in Bengal.

items.name: Wandiwash
items.detail: 1760: Eyre Coote defeats the French under Lally, ending French power in India.

items.name: Buxar
items.detail: 1764: the Company defeats Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II, and gets the diwani of Bengal the next year.

items.name: Seringapatam
items.detail: 1799: the Company defeats Tipu Sultan in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

items.name: Assaye
items.detail: 1803: Arthur Wellesley defeats the Maratha confederacy in the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

items.name: Sobraon
items.detail: 1846: the Company defeats the Sikh army, ending the First Anglo-Sikh War.

items.name: Kohima
items.detail: 1944: British and Indian troops hold Kohima against the Japanese army.

items.name: Imphal
items.detail: 1944: the Japanese offensive into India is stopped at Imphal.

items.name: Longewala
items.detail: 1971: a small Indian force holds a Pakistani tank column in the Thar desert until the air force arrives.

items.name: Kargil
items.detail: 1999: India retakes the heights above Kargil and Drass held by Pakistani troops.
